body: Use an append-only JSONL event stream and reviewed Markdown in Git. Build SQLite FTS5 only as a disposable index. This preserves diffs, provenance, portability, and recovery.
summary: Canonical project memory is Git-tracked text; databases are derived caches.
title: Use files and Git as the canonical memory

body: Expose the same local store through MCP stdio and a shell CLI. Model subscriptions can invoke the local tool without the memory layer calling OpenAI, Anthropic, or another model API.
summary: Use MCP plus CLI as provider-neutral access paths with no model API dependency.
title: Keep the project memory provider-neutral

body: AgentMemory exposes recall, timeline, provenance verification, explicit save, diagnostics, and retrieval evaluation. Reuse its interface and benchmark ideas first; do not adopt its full 54-tool surface or runtime until independently evaluated.
summary: AgentMemory is a high-value source for MCP ergonomics, timelines, provenance tools, and retrieval benchmarks.
title: Audit AgentMemory as an interface and evaluation reference

body: Graphiti retains raw episodes, traces derived facts to their sources, and represents changing facts with temporal validity. Its graph backend and LLM extraction pipeline are too heavy for the project-memory bootstrap, but its data semantics are directly relevant.
summary: Graphiti is a strong reference for provenance, temporal validity, episodes, and non-destructive supersession.
title: Audit Graphiti's temporal provenance model

body: Arousal, valence, novelty, threat, reward, surprise, and goal relevance may influence encoding, consolidation, retrieval, or forgetting in different ways. The system should test these as separable signals and must not infer that a scoring mechanism gives an LLM subjective feelings.
summary: Emotion-related appraisal signals may improve memory prioritization if evaluated separately and protected against manipulation.
title: Test emotional salience as multiple memory-control signals

body: Compare plain file search, SQLite FTS5, hybrid lexical-vector retrieval, temporal retrieval, and graph-assisted retrieval on a fixed corpus. Include Recall@k, MRR/nDCG, answer support, contradiction handling, provenance accuracy, harmful intrusion, p50/p95 latency, token overhead, disk growth, and recovery after corruption.
summary: Do not add semantic or graph complexity until it beats lexical baselines on a reproducible gold set.
title: Gate memory complexity with controlled retrieval evaluation

body: Unit tests cover add/search, document indexing, provenance, supersession, malformed events, concurrent writers, and MCP tool calls.
summary: Implemented and smoke-tested append-only project memory with SQLite FTS5, CLI, MCP stdio, Codex configuration, and Claude Code configuration; no model API is required.
title: Provider-neutral project memory bootstrap implemented

body: Adding 12 query families produced 1066 unique OpenAlex leads across 32 families, but spot checks exposed substantial query drift. The new records are discovered-unscreened and cannot support a completeness or review claim.
summary: The initial 684-work catalog used 20 human/agent query families and did not systematically cover animal, motor, skeletal-muscle, immune, transcriptional, non-neural, prokaryotic, or collective memory.
title: Comparative biological memory was absent from the initial discovery coverage

body: Shared use of the word memory does not establish shared substrate, computation, cognition, or subjective experience. Each mapping needs an empirical assay, substrate, timescale, simpler baseline, predicted benefit, failure mode, and rejection criterion.
summary: Animal episodic-like memory, motor learning, skeletal-muscle history, immune memory, transcriptional priming, CRISPR, non-neural habituation, and collective memory must remain separate research tracks.
title: Study biological memory as distinct mechanism families

body: Retrieval and reader evaluation remain separate. High-impact conclusions require independent challenge, blinded backend labels where feasible, retained negative runs, and clean-environment reproduction.
summary: Freeze evidence, corpus, metrics, budgets, and rejection rules; compare no-memory, rg, FTS5, dense, hybrid, temporal, graph, and salience one level at a time.
title: Use stage-gated research laboratory before product architecture

body: API workers may propose relevance labels, source cards, or candidate claims through structured outputs, but cannot directly promote accepted evidence. Admission requires a frozen pilot measuring locator accuracy, unsupported claims, abstention, reviewer time, cost, privacy, and provider failures. Local embeddings do not require a chat-model API.
summary: The project does not need a separate API agent for canonical memory or initial benchmarks; any future cloud model is a replaceable batch worker.
title: Keep model APIs optional and review-gated

body: The new tracks cover associative memory, continual learning, semantic compression, engram allocation, replay, neuromodulated memory, prospective offloading, metamemory, durable storage, temporal provenance, distributed memory, and information thermodynamics. Eleven broad queries returned 40 top records; the metamemory query returned only two and is recorded as query-failed rather than saturated. Query drift and zero independent review prevent evidence claims.
summary: The OpenAlex discovery catalog now contains 1464 unique records and 12 newly tracked interdisciplinary topics, but all new topic results remain unscreened.
title: Interdisciplinary discovery broadens the candidate mechanism space

body: Priority-A topics advance through cycles of screening, exact-locator primary reading, adversarial challenge, synthesis, and registered experiment. A checkpoint occurs after 25 screened records or three newly primary-read decisive sources in one topic. Final architecture selection remains blocked until baseline reproduction and independent review.
summary: Broad discovery and structured evidence processing will run in parallel; raw paper counts will not gate the first lexical benchmarks.
title: Begin reversible mechanism synthesis before global completeness

body: Test each signal through separate write, replay, retention, and retrieval ablations. Reject or restrict the approach if it creates chronic threat bias, emotional-language poisoning, quiet-critical-memory loss, false persistence after correction, or no held-out consequence-weighted gain. These signals are not evidence of subjective emotion.
summary: Separate consequence valence, magnitude, urgency, surprise, controllability, uncertainty, explicit user weight, and recurrence may improve memory control beyond relevance and recency.
title: Operational emotion should be decomposed before salience testing

summary: In a frozen 125-record DeepSeek V4 Flash candidate-screening run, all outputs passed schema validation but two records without abstracts violated the prompt rule and were marked include. A deterministic policy layer downgraded them. The worker is admitted only for candidate generation, never evidence promotion. Conservative cumulative API cost including pilots was USD 0.0613668 under the USD 10 cap.
title: DeepSeek screening requires deterministic guards

summary: On the 24-query PMLAB development slice, ripgrep and SQLite FTS5 both reached Recall@5 0.841 but had forbidden-record intrusion 0.292, zero abstention on unanswerable queries, and zero cross-language recall. This exploratory authored slice diagnoses the instrument and cannot select an architecture.
title: Raw lexical retrieval has safety and semantic gaps

summary: Keep the 24-query corpus as an instrument-development slice. Before calling PMLAB v0 ready or testing embeddings as an architecture candidate, create 120 split-by-history examples, obtain independent A/B labels and adjudication, audit leakage, freeze hashes, and rerun unchanged B0/B1/B2 rules.
title: Expand PMLAB only after independent annotation

summary: Deterministic DOI/OpenAlex identity checks resolved all 37 DeepSeek include candidates. Abstract-level screening found 35 distinct intellectual works: 19 priority full reads, 9 background sources, 6 deferred sources, 1 challenge-only preprint, plus 2 merged records (a version duplicate and an eLife decision-letter artifact). No additional model spending is justified until full-text extraction.
title: DeepSeek include queue reduces to nineteen priority reads

body: DeMem constrains runtime decision states rather than disk storage; the compaction survey reports illustrative repeated-summary loss; human/computational RDT models motivate task-weighted distortion; semantic completion demonstrates plausible unsupported reconstruction risk.
summary: Five full-text reads converge on distinguishing a reversible high-fidelity archive from lossy semantic representations and a query-conditioned bounded working set; this convergence does not independently validate one final architecture.
title: Compression evidence supports separating archive from active budget

body: The raw archive remains canonical. Semantic summaries cannot overwrite evidence. Emotion is initially factor-separated metadata rather than a scalar truth or anthropomorphic internal state.
summary: A lossless versioned episodic archive plus rebuildable provenance-bearing semantic hypotheses plus query-conditioned context may outperform either raw retrieval or rolling summaries, but must be rejected if benchmark gains do not survive cost and safety controls.
title: Three-tier archive semantic hypothesis and working-set design

summary: Before promotion, test repeated compaction, delayed model change versus noise, plausible semantic completion, and factor-separated emotional allocation under matched context budgets and explicit safety and cost gates.
title: Compression mechanisms require four preregistered benchmark families

body: This is an artifact availability block not a failed scientific reproduction. Recheck later versions and supplements. Keep all three result families below the independent-reproduction gate.
summary: The rate-distortion working-memory repository was located and pinned but lacks a dependency lockfile bundled referenced data and a detected license; no matching public DeMem repository or compaction-survey experiment repository was found in the 2026-08-22 artifact search.
title: Public code does not yet make compression claims reproducible

body: Stress can favor habit strategies; reward effects depended on task-relevant semantic contingency; novelty rescued weak rat spatial memory only within mechanistic timing conditions; limited context sampling produced overgeneralization in male mice; an LC review proposes an encoding-versus-retrieval shift.
summary: Five full-text sources separate stress/arousal reward contingency novelty prediction-related updating encoding coverage and timing; their effects include subsystem shifts specificity changes and bounded persistence rather than a universal memory-strength increase.
title: Emotion-related memory modulation is multidimensional and phase-specific

summary: Raw episodes should be appended immediately while promotion into derived semantic or procedural memory may use an expiring eligibility tag linked to verified outcomes; this must beat raw retrieval and immediate promotion without promoting unrelated novelty or poison.
title: Safe delayed consolidation uses append-now promote-later eligibility

summary: Evaluate false context generalization and habitual procedure perseveration in addition to weighted recall; factor valence arousal consequence surprise reliability timing contingency scope and required controller separately.
title: Emotion benchmarks must test specificity and subsystem shifts

body: Nadasdy et al. reported recurring CA1 spike sequences above several surrogate families and short ripple-associated sequences, but null-model choice is critical. Olafsdottir et al. reported local/congruent/forward replay near task movement and broader deep-MEC-coherent replay during disengagement; engaged content predicted choices, while key state-by-accuracy interactions were nonsignificant.
summary: Two fully read rat electrophysiology studies support time-compressed recurrence and task-state-dependent awake replay; neither proves that replay causes long-term consolidation, and the strongest pre/post sleep evidence in the 1999 study used two rats.
title: Replay content is state-dependent but causal function remains unresolved

body: This is an engineering translation, not a biological-equivalence claim. Reject it if raw archive retrieval is within two points, if gains vanish after compute matching, or if it worsens rare-event coverage, poison persistence, unsupported consolidation, or post-change procedural perseveration.
summary: Under a fixed maintenance budget, a small task-local contradiction-aware replay phase near decisions plus diverse offline replay may improve both immediate action and delayed transfer more than uniform, recency, relevance-only, diversity-only, or no replay.
title: Phase-conditioned replay should beat one global replay policy

body: Post-training disruption slowed one maze but the effect was moderate and disappeared with extra training. Awake SWR disruption impaired outbound history-dependent alternation while sparing inbound performance, place fields, and later rest reactivation. The evidence upgrades replay-associated processing to a serious candidate while leaving its content-specific mechanism unresolved.
summary: Two small rat perturbation studies causally link ripple-associated hippocampal activity to selected spatial-memory performance, but neither selectively manipulated decoded replay content.
title: Causal ripple disruption supports a processing window not replay content alone

body: This separates benefit from replayed content from benefit due to extra tokens, regularization, or another maintenance window. Cross simple tasks with history-dependent tasks and require a content-by-demand interaction before promotion.
summary: Every replay experiment must compare targeted content with no maintenance, sham calls, random real episodes, corrupted/irrelevant episodes, and direct just-in-time retrieval under equal compute.
title: Replay benchmarks require content-specific causal controls
